In the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma game-hosting platform), I need to understand the current architecture for per-game-family network ports, so I can build a fix: automatically create the correct PortForward DB rows for NAT (non-dedicated-IP) game servers at PROVISION time, instead of requiring the customer to manually add each one via the dashboard (which just caused a real customer outage — a Valheim customer only added 1 of the 3 UDP ports Valheim actually needs).

Please find and report on:
1. Where is the current "customer-facing game port" defined per family? A recent fix (commit 3be5383, from a game-catalog verify sweep) fixed 8 families where the wrong port (RCON/admin) was being shown as the customer's join port instead of the real game port. Find whatever module/constant/function defines "the real game port for family X" today — likely something like lib/game-ports.ts or a GAME_PORT map, used by both the health-check code (checkGamePortOpen in worker/provision-health.ts) and whatever surfaces the connect-address to the customer.
2. Is this mapping ONE port per family, or does it support multiple ports (protocol + port list)? Valheim needs 3 consecutive UDP ports (2456-2458); Minecraft needs 1 TCP port for the game plus a separate RCON TCP port that must NOT be customer-forwarded (per the RCON-exposure security fix, commit 196e5c9, which explicitly retracts admin/RCON port auto-forwards). Check how that retraction logic distinguishes "the real game port" from "the RCON/admin port" — I need the same family-by-family port classification for building auto-forwarding of ONLY the real game ports.
3. Where in worker/index.ts does provision() currently handle NAT vs dedicated-IP servers, and where does it currently NOT create any PortForward rows for the game port on a NAT server (confirmed in an earlier investigation this session: "only SSH gets an automatic port-forward at provision time... the game's own port is forwarded only if the customer adds a PortForward — a separate, pre-existing product gap")? I need the exact insertion point to add automatic PortForward creation for NAT servers right after/during provisioning, for every game family, using each family's correct guest port(s) and protocol(s) from the mapping found in step 1/2.
4. Look at lib/actions-server.ts's addPortForward action (the customer-facing one) for the exact port-allocation pattern (MAX_FORWARDS_PER_SERVER limit, collision-safe allocation loop across PF_MIN..PF_MAX) I should reuse/mirror for the automatic provision-time version, so behavior stays consistent (same public port range, same collision handling, same job types queued afterward — SYNC_FORWARDS, SYNC_GAME_DNS).
5. Confirm: does a DEDICATED-IP server need any of this at all, or does it just work automatically once it has its own public IP (i.e., this fix should apply ONLY to NAT/shared-IP servers)?

Report concisely under 500 words with file:line citations. Investigation only — do not modify any files.

Author: Nxeon <haxkodi@gmail.com>

    Forward the port players actually join on, not the RCON port
    
    lib/games.ts's GAME_PORT is a health-CHECK map: where an image exposes a TCP
    port it prefers that one, because a TCP connect is real evidence the game
    process bound it. Provisioning reused it as a forward-this-port map. Those are
    different questions, and for eight families GAME_PORT names an RCON/query/admin
    port — its own inline comments have always said so:
    
      rust 28016/tcp -> joins on 28015/udp      ark 27020/tcp -> 7777/udp
      projectzomboid 27015/tcp -> 16261/udp     factorio 27015/tcp -> 34197/udp
      arkasa 27020/tcp -> 7777/udp              soulmask 18888/tcp -> 8777/udp
      squad 21114/tcp -> 7787/udp               kf2 8080/tcp -> 7777/udp
    
    Confirmed live on a fresh Rust provision: the guest listened on both 28015/udp
    and 28016/tcp, node-2's NAT held exactly one game rule (28016/tcp), and the
    dashboard handed the customer their RCON port as the address to give players.
    Every NAT game server of those eight families was unjoinable from handover.
    
    This is the same outage found on the real paying customer rust-w75hko during the
    node-2 migration, diagnosed then as "allocateGameForward was never called for
    it". It is called — with the wrong port.
    
    Fix: joinPortFor() + a GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE table of exactly those eight,
    every entry sourced from the family's own `docker run -p` mapping in
    prisma/catalog.ts / seed-wave*-games.ts and cross-checked against the join port
    GAME_PORT's comment already named. Provisioning allocates a second forward when
===196e5c9===
commit 196e5c97f10b96aadc940c29633de09ab5eeb65a
Author: Nxeon <haxkodi@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Sep 6 06:22:04 2026 +0000

    Stop leaving game RCON/admin ports published to the internet
    
    Follow-on from the join-port fix, found by asking what was actually listening on
    the port provisioning had been publishing. Rust's WebSocket RCON answered a
    connection from off-box and returned a full serverinfo dump, using the password
    `docker` — didstopia/rust-server bakes `+rcon.password docker` into its launch
    line and prisma/catalog.ts never overrides it. That is ban/kick/any-convar/wipe
    control of a customer's server, reachable from the internet, on the same port
    the dashboard was telling them to hand to their players.
    
    The other seven admin-port families have the same shape (ark and projectzomboid
    both seed changeme12 for ADMIN_PASSWORD/RCON_PASSWORD).
    
    Blast radius was zero, narrowly: the only real customer in these families
    (rust-w75hko) predates auto-forwarding and holds only its join port — checked
    from the DB, without touching their server. The next order of any of the eight
    would have been exposed.
    
    Fix: retract the check-only forward once it has served its purpose. A
    non-primary node still must publish game.port to check through it — that is the
    only path there — but once the check passes and the join forward exists, the
    admin forward is deleted and the NAT re-synced, leaving exactly SSH + the join
    port. Nothing internal regresses: lib/game-control.ts tunnels RCON to
    127.0.0.1:<port> over SSH and never used the public forward. A customer who
    wants remote RCON can still add it from the dashboard, deliberately.

I have everything needed. Here's the report.

## Report

**1. The "real join port" mapping — `lib/games.ts`**
- `GAME_PORT` (`lib/games.ts:148-251`): a **health-check** map, `Record<GameFamily, {port, protocol}>` — one entry per family, preferring a TCP port when the image exposes one (proof-of-life for the check), even when that TCP port is RCON/query/admin.
- `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE` (`lib/games.ts:281-317`): a `Partial<Record<...>>` for the 15 families (the 8 from 3be5383 plus later Source-engine/sdtd finds) whose join port differs from `GAME_PORT`.
- `joinPortFor(family)` (`lib/games.ts:325-327`): `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE[family] ?? GAME_PORT[family]` — **the** function to call for "what should be forwarded / shown to the customer." Used by `worker/index.ts`, `worker/game-subdomain-sync.ts:97`, and `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:93`.
- `checkGamePortOpen`/`gamePortForServer` in `worker/provision-health.ts:92-98,328` consume `GAME_PORT` only (the check port), never `joinPortFor`.

**2. Single port only — no multi-port support today.** Every entry in both `GAME_PORT` and `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE` is exactly one `{port, protocol}` pair; `joinPortFor` returns one pair. `valheim: { port: 2456, protocol: "udp" }` (`lib/games.ts:150`) has no override, so `joinPortFor("valheim")` yields only 2456/udp — even though `prisma/catalog.ts:329` provisions the container with `-p 2456-2458:2456-2458/udp` (3 consecutive UDP ports). **This is the actual gap**: there is no port-list/range concept anywhere in this mapping, so any fix must add one (e.g. a family → `{port,protocol}[]` table, or a `basePort`+`count` shape) rather than reuse `joinPortFor` as-is for multi-port families.

**3. `worker/index.ts` provision() — NAT auto-forward already exists, but single-port.** Two additive blocks, both gated `!SANDBOX && !dedicated`:
- Lines 1110-1125: on a non-primary node only, forwards `game.port`/`game.protocol` (the check port) via `allocateGameForward`, to make the health check reachable.
- Lines 1186-1203 (from commit 3be5383): resolves `join = joinPortFor(joinFam)` and, if no existing `PortForward` for that `{guestPort, protocol}`, calls `allocateGameForward(server.nodeId, server.id, join.port, join.protocol)` then `syncPortForwardsBestEffort`. Runs for **all** NAT nodes (not just non-primary), unconditionally per family.
- Lines 1222-1234 (commit 196e5c9): retracts the check-port forward afterward if it was admin-only (`checkPortIsAdminOnly`).
- **Insertion point for the fix**: replace/extend the single `allocateGameForward(..., join.port, join.protocol)` call at line 1195 with a loop over a new multi-port list for the family (e.g. `joinPortsFor(family)` returning `{port,protocol}[]`), calling `allocateGameForward` once per port, each independently checked for an existing row via the same `db.portForward.findFirst` pattern (lines 1191-1194) before allocating. One `syncPortForwardsBestEffort` call after the loop is sufficient.
- Confirms your prior finding was about the *original* gap this same commit closed for single-port families — multi-port (Valheim, and any other 2+ consecutive-port family) is still unaddressed.

**4. Allocation pattern to reuse: already two patterns exist, and worker/index.ts already uses the right one.**
- Customer-facing `addPortForward` (`lib/actions-server.ts:254-329`): `MAX_FORWARDS_PER_SERVER = 10` (line 252), scans `PF_MIN..PF_MAX` (`SSH_PORT_START`/`END`, `lib/ipam.ts:24-25`, global not per-node) for up to 8 free candidates (line 286), retry-insert on `P2002` (lines 298-310), then queues `SYNC_FORWARDS` + `SYNC_GAME_DNS` jobs (lines 319, 323).
- Provisioning already uses `allocateGameForward` (`lib/ipam.ts:337-370`) instead — a transactional, advisory-locked, per-node-range allocator (`ipamRange(nodeId)`) with its own retry loop (`CLAIM_ATTEMPTS`). This is the correct one to keep reusing for the multi-port fix (already the pattern at `worker/index.ts:1195`); no need to port over `addPortForward`'s scan logic. `SYNC_FORWARDS`/`SYNC_GAME_DNS` job creation should stay the same (`syncPortForwardsBestEffort` inline call + one `SYNC_GAME_DNS` job at line 1239, already unconditional after the game-port block).
- `MAX_FORWARDS_PER_SERVER` is customer-facing only and not currently checked in the provisioning path — worth deciding whether auto-created rows should count against/be exempt from that limit if a customer later adds more.

**5. Dedicated-IP confirmed exempt.** Every forward/allocation block is gated `!dedicated` (lines 1112, 1189, 1222; also `lib/ipam.ts:333-335`'s own doc comment: "Dedicated-IP servers need no forward (their guest port IS the public port) — callers should only call this for the NAT case."). A dedicated-IP server's guest port is directly reachable on its own public IP with no NAT/PortForward row at all — this fix should apply only inside the `!dedicated` branches, exactly where the existing single-port logic already lives.
